_readme: Sensor manifest imported from a KiCad board that OpenTac-CAD did not generate (see 'source'). Same keys and meanings as an OpenTac-CAD export; lengths in mm.
Frame is Y-UP, rotated so the cable tail points down; x=0 is the connector, y=0 the lowest point of the board edge. 'outline', 'edge_cuts' and 'pixels' overlay directly.
'edge_cuts' is the manufactured board edge, curves flattened to <=0.1 mm segments. There is no separately drawn shape for a board made outside OpenTac-CAD, so 'outline' is the same ring.
'pixels' is [x, y, row_index, col_index] per taxel, at the taxel copper centre, and is the authority on where taxels sit.
'w'/'h' are one taxel's copper bounding box, read from its footprint. If 'pixel_rot_deg' is non-zero, every taxel is rotated by that angle (CCW) about its centre in this frame.

Scan order is OpenTac-CAD's: row_index/col_index are the rank of the net's connector pad among the row (column) pads, in ascending pad order - not the net name's number, not position. 'rp'/'cp' are those pad numbers; 'rn'/'cn' the net names in the same order. Pads are numbered by position in OpenTac-CAD's convention - pad 1 at the left end with the tail down, seen from the top - because that is how the readout meets them. Where the board's footprint numbers them otherwise, its own numbers are in 'rp_footprint'/'cp_footprint'.
'ox'/'oy'/'px'/'py' are derived exactly as OpenTac-CAD derives them, for older MCU code. They are not geometry and on a hand-laid board ox+ci*px will not reproduce positions. Use 'pixels'.

'shear' groups taxels that share a bump: 2x2 blocks assigned on a uniform grid, pairing lattice rows and columns from the grid's edge. The layout has no gaps to recover them from; the grouping comes from the bump sheet. 'shear.bumps' are block centres; 'shear.b' is parallel to 'pixels' and gives each taxel's block, or -1 if none. Shear direction is the differential within a block, signed by (pixel - bump centre).
